Sources & editing

Gloss. Uses ORACC’s annotation for each word in this inscription, with English inflections checked against the ORACC and Schaudig clauses. This is an editorial gloss, not a published expert interlinear. Competing interpretations stay available in word details.

Alignment. Word links and typeset spacing are project decisions. The reader adds restoration brackets on seven lines and removes a duplicated “my” in line 27. The selected word’s notes retain the imported wording and reasons for changes.

Cylinder locator

The finished print’s leveled handcopy includes the Yale fragment and the selected tablet patches. Its paper join is opposite the hatch, between lines 25 and 26. The black line marks the text boundary between lines 45 and 1. Both cap inscriptions reuse the final printed artwork: Hebrew at the left, Pasargadae at the right, with their tops pointing toward line 1.

Reading guide
[…] / [word]
Missing signs / proposed restoration. Brackets are complete within each cell; the gloss brackets the whole word if any sign is restored.
⸢word⸣
Damaged signs that can still be read.
x
An unidentified sign. Consecutive fragments are grouped.
?
An uncertain reading, meaning or syntax. Unmarked words are not guaranteed certain.
T / •
Text supplied by a tablet witness: T for English, a dot for cuneiform. Tap either for its source; tablet origin alone does not imply uncertainty.
English
A dotted underline flags an uncertain word mapping. Dashed connections mark damaged, missing or uncertain signs.
Transliteration conventions
Uncertain passages
ORACC counts

Bars count annotated meanings, not phrases from English translations. The highlighted meaning is ORACC’s annotation for this word; the reader’s inflected gloss and Finkel’s English may differ.

Entries match by lemma, dictionary guideword and part of speech. Counts include all indexed Akkadian periods and dialects, including overlapping editions. Frequency is not translation confidence.

Filters all charts. Damaged and questioned readings remain included.

Dataset & counting method

Uses the contextual sense (SENSE), falling back to the dictionary guideword when none is supplied. Different guidewords and parts of speech stay separate; source labels and possible editorial errors are retained.

ORACC’s sense definitions ↗

Controls

Off: only hovered or selected matches across numbered lines. On: all matches, including within a line.

Text layers
Tap to toggle a layer. Hold any layer button, or press Shift+Enter on it, to show all four; if all are on, hide all. The cylinder has separate Original and Translation controls.
Word details
Tap a word to highlight its match; tap again for details. While details are open, another cuneiform word switches the panel. English or × closes it. A background tap keeps it open.
Previous / next word
Use ← / → with details open, or swipe right / left inside the panel. A vertical swipe scrolls.
Line number
Tap to advance, or drag up/down and release to jump. When focused, use arrow keys; Home / End go to the first / last line.
Cylinder
Drag up toward later line numbers; drag sideways to look toward either end. There is no roll, and yaw stops at ±85°. Right-click, or hold still on touch, to put line 1 at the top with upright caps. Tap the handwriting or a line number to select it. Pinch, scroll, or use + / − to zoom. With two fingers or Shift-drag, sideways movement pans along the cylinder and vertical movement still rotates it. The camera stays level with the cylinder axis. Selecting a word smoothly turns, centers, and zooms to its location; Center or Home repeats this. With the view focused, arrow keys turn and Shift+F10 resets rotation. On a phone, the Text and Cylinder tabs switch between full-screen views.
